samples.summary: Many stderr error-envelope emitters bypass `outputError`, so they still print pretty-printed multi-line JSON with no `command` — breaking the one-line/attributed contract this change documents and tests
samples.evidence: The diff makes `outputError` emit a single line with `command` and the test asserts `expect(raw).not.toContain('\n')` (test/output.test.ts:148). But error envelopes are also written directly on real failure paths, all with `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)` and no `command`: docs.ts:195 and docs.ts:255 (backend-shaped error on `docs content` / `docs export`), notes.ts:148, notes.ts:203, slides.ts:154, slides.ts:204, schema.ts:32 (`{"error":{"code":"NOT_FOUND"...}}` for `wafflebase schema <unknown>`), files/upload.ts:217 and files/upload.ts:227 (`errorJson`), files/download.ts:57, docs/import.ts:164/194/211, notes/import.ts:159/188/212, slides/import.ts:194/237/254. A caller following docs/design/cli.md §9 ("Errors: a single JSON line on stderr ... command") with a line-delimited parser sees a multi-line, unattributed body for these — i.e. the very backend-error cases the feature is meant to attribute. The new tests only cover the `outputError` path, so nothing catches it.

samples.summary: `runCli` mutates the caller-supplied program by registering a new `preAction` hook on every invocation
samples.evidence: `program.hook('preAction', ...)` is registered inside `runCli` on the `program` parameter. Called twice with the same `Command` instance (a supported signature — tests pass a program in at test/output.test.ts:423 and :447), the hook list grows each call, and the hook outlives `runCli` while still capturing the previous call's `acting` closure. Registering the hook in `buildProgram`, or tracking the acting command without mutating a shared object, avoids the accumulating side effect on a parameter.

samples.summary: No `command` attribution for failures raised before any action runs (option/argument parsing, unknown command), which is a common agent-facing failure class
samples.evidence: `acting` is only assigned by the `preAction` hook, which commander fires immediately before an action handler. Anything thrown during option parsing, argument coercion, or a `preSubcommand` hook leaves `acting === undefined`, so the envelope omits `command` even though commander knows exactly which subcommand was being parsed (the failing command is available via commander's error/hook context). The code comments call this "omitted rather than guessed", but for a parse-time failure the command is known, not guessed — the attribution gap is silent.

finding.summary: Many stderr error-envelope emitters bypass `outputError`, so they still print pretty-printed multi-line JSON with no `command` — breaking the one-line/attributed contract this change documents and tests

But error envelopes are also written directly on real failure paths, all with `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)` and no `command`: docs.ts:195 and docs.ts:255 (backend-shaped error on `docs content` / `docs export`), notes.ts:148, notes.ts:203, slides.ts:154, slides.ts:204, schema.ts:32 (`{"error":{"code":"NOT_FOUND"...}}` for `wafflebase schema <unknown>`), files/upload.ts:217 and files/upload.ts:227 (`errorJson`), files/download.ts:57, docs/import.ts:164/194/211, notes/import.ts:159/188/212, slides/import.ts:194/237/254. A caller following docs/design/cli.md §9 ("Errors: a single JSON line on stderr ... command") with a line-delimited parser sees a multi-line, unattributed body for these — i.e. the very backend-error cases the feature is meant to attribute. verdict.reason: Every cited location exists as described. formatter.ts:80-93 emits a one-line envelope with `command` and explicitly documents that contract (docs/design/cli.md:1017-1018), and the new tests assert one-line-ness (test/output.test.ts:151, :339). But docs.ts:191-198 and docs.ts:252-258 intercept `!res.ok` with a backend `error` body, print `JSON.stringify(body, null, 2)` (multi-line, no `command`), set exitCode and `return` — so the enclosing `catch { outputError(e, this) }` never runs. The same bypass exists at notes.ts:148/203, slides.ts:154/204, schema.ts:32-40, files/upload.ts:217/227, files/download.ts:57, and the three import modules. No guard or caller makes these unreachable; they are the ordinary backend-error paths (TYPE_MISMATCH is even named in the Error Matrix at cli.md:1028), so a line-delimited stderr parser following the documented contract mis-parses real failures and loses attribution. Real, reachable, in the correctness lane (broken documented invariant / inconsistent error handling).

finding.summary: The new "one line per error, with `command`" stderr invariant is broken by the sibling error paths that bypass `outputError`
finding.evidence: `outputError` now emits a single-line envelope with `command` (formatter.ts:83-91) and the tests assert `expect(raw).not.toContain('\n')`. But several real error paths never go through `outputError` and still emit pretty-printed, multi-line JSON with no `command` field: docs.ts:195 and docs.ts:255 (backend-shaped error on `docs content` / `docs export`, e.g. TYPE_MISMATCH), notes.ts:148 and notes.ts:203, slides.ts:154 and slides.ts:204, schema.ts:32 (`Unknown command`), plus the import/upload helpers (docs/import.ts:164,194,201,211,245; notes/import.ts:159,188,197,212; slides/import.ts:194,237,244,254,312; files/upload.ts:217,227; files/download.ts:57) which all use `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)`. A caller that follows the newly documented contract and reads stderr with a line-delimited parser will fail on these — the very paths the change claims to make attributable. Nothing in the change guards or migrates them.

verdict.reason: The finding's evidence is accurate in this repository. `outputError` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:80-93) now emits a compact single-line envelope with an optional `command` field, and its doc comment (formatter.ts:66-73) plus the test at packages/cli/test/output.test.ts:148-151 (`expect(raw).not.toContain('\n')`) establish "one line per error, line-delimited parseable" as a tested contract. The sibling error branches bypass it exactly as claimed: packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:190-199 and docs.ts:252-259 emit `console.error(JSON.stringify(body, null, 2))` and `return` before the `catch { outputError(e, this) }` at docs.ts:213/319 can run, producing multi-line pretty JSON with no `command` on a real path (backend-shaped errors such as TYPE_MISMATCH from `getDocContent`). The same pattern is present at notes.ts:148, notes.ts:203, slides.ts:154, slides.ts:204, schema.ts:32-40, docs/import.ts:164/194/211, notes/import.ts:159/188/212, slides/import.ts:194/237/254, files/upload.ts:217/227, files/download.ts:57. No guard, wrapper, or caller routes these through `outputError`, so `already-guarded` fails; the code is literally as described, so `not-present` fails. The task file's scope note (docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-error-envelope-command-todo.md:19-22) defers these to #654/#655, but that is author intent, not a lens-based exclusion, and the rubric explicitly counts defects at untouched locations. A caller following the newly documented stderr contract will hit unparseable multi-line output on these paths, which is a real behavioral inconsistency within the correctness lane (broken invariant), so I cannot refute.
